main_body: Tall brick townhouse: slate mansard roof with a zinc flat top, a dormer and a chimney, over three brick storeys with stone-framed windows, a balcony and a green door
top_band: Rows 17-23 (7 rows) of light grey-green zinc (L=122 then 95), above the slate slope rows 24-43 (L 53-134). The orange cornice line at row 44 closes it before the brick face.
evidence: The roof reads as a real roof surface. A light flat top band and a long textured slate slope (about 27 rows together) sit above the front face. A distinct orange cornice row (row 44) is the front-edge line, with darker rows 46-47 beneath it as the eave shadow. The brick facade below is about 99 rows tall. Its windows have stone surrounds and sills, and the balcony and door pediment project forward. This matches the roof-over-wall structure of the references, so it is not a front elevation with a hat.

style.evidence: The brick, slate and stone have 4-5 value steps each and some grain, so the interior shading is decent. The measured facts show a sticker-like outline: 97% of dark edge pixels are neutral, against 7-9% for the references, and the outline colour #1d1722 is almost colourless. The references use tinted dark-material outlines. The candidate also has far fewer distinct colours (47 against 185 and 66). Colours per tile (14) and flat-fill coverage (2%) are comparable to the references. The near-black outline and lower colour variety make it look flatter than the Beodeul standard.
